title: feat(contracts): handle and validate contract IDs
problem: Contract IDs are not handled as a first-class type, so users pass raw strings around.
why: Contracts are the unit of Soroban work; IDs must be validated and normalized consistently.
context: `stellar-strkey` supports contract strkeys and contract ID parsing exists at the XDR level.
scope: Add a validated ContractId type that accepts strkey or hex forms
Normalize output and report the accepted input form
out_of_scope: Resolving a contract ID to a WASM hash over the network.
acceptance: Contract IDs validate and normalize deterministically
docs: Document accepted forms in the contracts guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): discover and validate WASM containers
problem: There is no way to load a WASM file and confirm it is a well-formed container before inspecting it.
why: Validating the container is the safe first step before parsing custom sections.
context: Contract spec extraction (a separate issue) needs a validated container.
scope: Detect the WASM magic and version, and enforce a size limit
Report the result without executing the module
guidance: Never interpret or run the module; parse structure only.
acceptance: Valid containers are accepted; malformed ones are rejected with clear errors
tests: Tests with a valid fixture and truncated/invalid inputs
security: Bound size; treat WASM as untrusted.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): cache extracted contract specs
problem: Spec extraction would be repeated for the same WASM.
why: Caching avoids duplicate work in multi-command workflows.
context: Spec extraction is a separate issue.
scope: Add an opt-in cache keyed by content hash
Bound cache size and document invalidation
guidance: Cache only derived metadata, never raw secrets.
acceptance: Cache hits avoid re-extraction and are bounded
tests: Unit tests for keys and eviction
security: Do not cache untrusted content indefinitely.
performance: This is the optimization; measure it.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): represent contract invocations
problem: Invocation operations (host function calls) have no representation.
why: Invocations are how contracts are called; representing them enables analysis and reporting.
scope: Represent an invocation's contract, function, and arguments
Render arguments with the curated SCVal renderer
guidance: Report only what the XDR contains.
acceptance: Invocations render with contract, function, and arguments
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): inspect contract instance storage
problem: Contract instance storage cannot be inspected.
why: Instance storage holds contract configuration and is commonly examined during debugging.
context: Instance entries are returned by RPC ledger-entry lookups.
scope: Decode a contract instance ledger entry and render its storage map
Distinguish instance data from other entries
guidance: Render keys and values with the curated renderer; bound output.
acceptance: Instance storage renders for a fixture contract
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): inspect persistent and temporary storage entries
problem: Persistent and temporary contract data entries cannot be inspected.
why: Storage durability and TTL are central Soroban concepts developers must observe.
context: Entries expose their durability and live-until ledger.
scope: Decode persistent and temporary entries with their TTL fields
Report durability explicitly
guidance: Report TTL as observed, not as a recommendation.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): map contract events to spec types
problem: Contract events are decoded generically without using the contract spec.
why: Using the spec turns cryptic values into labelled, typed output.
context: Contract spec extraction and event decoding are separate issues.
scope: Match event topics/data to spec entries when a spec is available
Fall back to generic decoding and label the fallback
out_of_scope: Guaranteeing a match; specs may be absent.
guidance: Never present inferred types as confirmed; label inference.
acceptance: Events render with spec types when present, and clearly without when absent
tests: Tests with and without a spec
deps: WASM spec extraction issue and event normalization issue.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): report contract environment and protocol compatibility
problem: It is unclear which Soroban environment/protocol a contract targets.
why: Compatibility information helps avoid deploying contracts against an incompatible protocol.
context: Contract metadata and the environment host interface version are observable from the WASM.
scope: Report observable environment/protocol metadata
State explicitly what cannot be determined
acceptance: Environment metadata is reported with limitations
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(contracts): add the contract inspection CLI command
problem: Contract inspection has no CLI entry point.
why: A CLI command makes the inspection work usable without writing code.
context: The CLI exposes decoding commands but nothing contract-specific.
scope: Add a `contract` command that inspects a local WASM file
Support terminal and JSON output
guidance: Fail closed on missing files; never fetch over the network.
acceptance: The command inspects a fixture WASM and prints results
security: Treat the WASM path as untrusted; bound size.
docs: Document in docs/CLI.md and the contracts guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(events): add event filtering by contract and topics
problem: Events cannot be filtered by contract or topics beyond passing raw filters.
why: Filtering is essential to focus on relevant events and reduce payload size.
context: getEvents accepts filters; there is no typed filter builder.
scope: Add a typed filter builder for contract IDs and topic segments
Validate filters before sending
guidance: Keep filters faithful to the RPC schema.
docs: Document filtering in the events guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(events): decode diagnostic events distinctly
problem: Diagnostic events are not separated from contract events.
why: Diagnostic events are for debugging and must not be conflated with application events.
context: Diagnostic events appear in transaction meta.
scope: Decode and label diagnostic events distinctly
Render them with the curated renderer
guidance: Label clearly; do not treat diagnostics as application data.
acceptance: Diagnostic events are labelled and rendered
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(events): normalize events into a stable structure
problem: Contract events have no normalized representation across sources.
why: Normalization enables correlation, filtering, and stable output.
context: Events arrive from RPC and from transaction meta.
scope: Define a normalized event structure with source, contract, topics, data, and ledger
Populate it from both sources
guidance: Keep the structure additive and documented.
acceptance: Both sources produce the same normalized shape
docs: Document the structure in the events guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(events): correlate events with their transaction
problem: Events and transactions are shown independently.
why: Correlation answers the common question of which transaction produced an event.
context: RPC events and meta events both carry transaction context.
scope: Attach transaction hash and ledger context to normalized events
Provide a lookup helper
guidance: Only correlate when the data is present.
acceptance: Events carry transaction context when available
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(ledger): add ledger sequence and close-time helpers
problem: Ledger sequence and close-time handling is ad hoc.
why: Ledger context is needed for event windows and diagnostics.
context: getLatestLedger reports sequence and close time.
scope: Add helpers to compute close-time from a ledger and to format ledger ranges
Use them in event tooling
guidance: Document the approximate close-time model; it is an estimate.
tests: Unit tests for ranges and estimates
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: test(events): add event fixture generation tooling
why: Tooling to generate fixtures makes event tests easy to add and review.
context: Fixture infrastructure is a separate issue.
scope: Add a small tool that encodes a described event into base64 XDR for fixtures
Never require network access
acceptance: Generated fixtures load and assert in tests
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.
